```{r setup, echo=F}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

# Results of Analysis/05_lag_analysis.R (nothing is fitted in this notebook)
res <- readRDS(here::here(params$results_path))
fig <- function(x) knitr::include_graphics(here::here("figures", x))
```

Lag is the time between the weather exposure and the cholera outcome, as extracted from
each study (`lag_days`), grouped into classes: no lag, 1 week, 2 weeks, 1, 2 and 3 months,
and more than 3 months. Estimates with a negative lag (exposure after outcome) or no stated
lag are counted in the first table and left out afterwards. Figures and models are for
cholera incidence, where almost all lagged estimates are.

# Lag information available

```{r coverage-status}
res$coverage_status %>%
  filter(out_class_metric != "other") %>%
  mutate(cell = str_glue("{n_estimates} ({n_studies})")) %>%
  select(exp_class, out_class_metric, lag_status, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lag_status, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0") %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "exp_class") %>%
  cols_label(out_class_metric = "Outcome") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Estimates (studies) by availability of lag information")
```

```{r coverage-lag}
res$coverage_lag %>%
  filter(out_class_metric == "incidence") %>%
  mutate(cell = str_glue("{n_estimates} ({n_studies})")) %>%
  select(exp_class, lag_class, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lag_class, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0", names_sort = TRUE) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(exp_class = "Exposure") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Estimates (studies) by lag class, incidence")
```

# Direction of estimates by lag

```{r fig-share, out.width="100%"}
fig("lag_share_positive.png")
```

```{r dir-table}
res$dir_by_lag %>%
  filter(out_class_metric == "incidence") %>%
  select(exp_class, lag_class, n_studies, n_pos, n_neg, n_none, frac_pos, frac_pos_lo, frac_pos_hi) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "exp_class") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("frac"), decimals = 2) %>%
  cols_merge(columns = c(frac_pos, frac_pos_lo, frac_pos_hi), pattern = "{1} ({2}-{3})") %>%
  cols_label(lag_class = "Lag", n_studies = "Studies", n_pos = "Positive", n_neg = "Negative",
             n_none = "None", frac_pos = "Share positive (95% CI)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Direction of estimates by lag, incidence") %>%
  tab_footnote("Share among positive and negative estimates; Wilson interval ignoring clustering by study.")
```

## By temporal resolution of the outcome

"No lag" covers different time spans depending on the resolution of the outcome data: with
monthly or yearly data it still spans weeks to months.

```{r fig-counts, out.width="100%"}
fig("lag_direction_counts.png")
```

```{r dir-res-table}
res$dir_by_lag_res %>%
  filter(out_class_metric == "incidence", exp_class %in% c("precipitation", "temperature")) %>%
  mutate(cell = str_glue("{n_pos}/{n_dir}")) %>%
  select(exp_class, out_res, lag_class, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lag_class, values_from = cell, values_fill = "-", names_sort = TRUE) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "exp_class") %>%
  cols_label(out_res = "Outcome resolution") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Positive / directional estimates by lag and outcome resolution, incidence")
```

# Study-level votes by lag

One vote per study, exposure and lag class, using the rule of the manuscript
(70% of directional estimates in one direction, otherwise uncertain).

```{r votes}
res$votes_by_lag %>%
  filter(out_class_metric == "incidence") %>%
  select(exp_class, lag_class, higher, lower, uncertain, p_binom) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "exp_class") %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_binom, decimals = 3) %>%
  sub_missing() %>%
  cols_label(lag_class = "Lag", higher = "Higher", lower = "Lower", uncertain = "Uncertain",
             p_binom = "p (sign test)") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Study-level votes by lag, incidence")
```

# Within-study lag profiles

Studies that report two or more lag classes for the same exposure.

```{r fig-profiles, out.width="80%"}
fig("lag_within_study_profiles.png")
```

```{r profile-summary}
res$profile_summary %>%
  filter(out_class_metric == "incidence") %>%
  count(exp_class, profile) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = profile, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(exp_class = "Exposure") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Number of studies by lag profile, incidence")
```

# Lag model

Bernoulli-logit model of the probability that an estimate is positive, with lag class and
outcome resolution (up to 14 days vs longer) as covariates, a study random effect and
estimate-level overdispersion: the Stan model of the main direction meta-regression
(`Analysis/stan/direction_meta_analysis_lag.stan`, a copy with the prior sd of the
coefficients passed as data). Fitted to precipitation and temperature, incidence,
national and sub-national estimates with a stated lag. "1 week" and "2 weeks" are merged.
The second row of the figure keeps only studies with two or more lag classes.

Each model is fitted with two priors on the coefficients: `N(0, 0.5)`, as in the main
meta-regression, and a wider `N(0, 1.5)`. The tight prior pulls modelled probabilities
towards the overall mean, away from the observed shares (red crosses) in small lag classes;
the wide prior follows the data more closely, with wider intervals.

```{r model-check, eval=!is.null(res$models)}
res$models$diagnostics %>%
  gt() %>%
  fmt_number(columns = max_rhat, decimals = 3) %>%
  tab_header(title = "Model fits")
```

```{r fig-model, out.width="100%", eval=!is.null(res$models)}
fig("lag_model_prob_positive.png")
```

```{r model-or, eval=!is.null(res$models)}
res$models$odds_ratios %>%
  filter(what == "lag_class_model") %>%
  mutate(cell = str_glue("{round(mean, 2)} ({round(q2.5, 2)}-{round(q97.5, 2)})")) %>%
  mutate(prior = str_glue("N(0, {sd_beta})")) %>%
  select(exp_class, subset, prior, strata, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = strata, values_from = cell) %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "exp_class") %>%
  cols_label(subset = "Studies", prior = "Prior") %>%
  tab_header(title = "Odds ratio of a positive association vs no lag (95% CrI)")
```
